items.t: Deer Lake Place is the small residential pocket at the west end of Deer Lake in central Burnaby, off Deer Lake Parkway near Gilpin Street, beside Burnaby's civic and cultural precinct at Deer Lake Park. The City publishes no street-by-street written boundary for the MLS® sub-area — exact boundary streets: UNVERIFIED. City use of "Deer Lake Place" as a neighbourhood name was not confirmed; the name is also a street / complex naming in the pocket.

Edges and neighbours: Canada Way to the north, Gilpin Street connecting the pocket south toward Kingsway, Deer Lake and Deer Lake Park to the east, Buckingham Heights on the slope south-east of the lake, Burnaby Hospital to the north-west, and Garden Village and Metrotown to the south-west. Burnaby City Hall is at 4949 Canada Way, just north-west of the pocket.
Where the condo stock concentrates: nowhere — there is none on the current record.

Transit: there is no SkyTrain station inside the pocket; Metrotown Station (Expo Line), south-west, is the nearest station named in the research. Specific bus route numbers for Deer Lake Parkway / Gilpin Street: UNVERIFIED.

blocks.text: Good to know about Deer Lake Place

items.t: Four sub-areas share one lake, and mixing them corrupts a price opinion. Say plainly which pocket a home is actually in.

The boardwalk closure runs to winter 2027. The section of boardwalk by the Deer Lake boat launch closed September 21, 2026 for a full replacement, with completion scheduled by winter 2027 and a signed detour via Sperling Avenue and Deer Lake Drive (about five extra minutes of walking); part of the nearby picnic area is also closed during construction.

The in-pocket school is not the public school. Deer Lake SDA School at 5550 Gilpin St is an independent school on the Province's list — a buyer assuming it is the SD41 catchment school for a Gilpin Street address would be wrong; the public catchment is set by the SD41 locator, address by address.

This is the city's government-and-culture precinct. Burnaby City Hall (4949 Canada Way) sits just north-west of the pocket and Burnaby Hospital (3935 Kincaid St) immediately north-west across the Burnaby Hospital sub-area — civic and hospital traffic patterns come with the west-end-of-the-lake setting.
The park's 2026 events calendar is a selling season fact.

Shopping runs to Metrotown, not to a local mall. There is no enclosed mall or shopping centre inside the pocket; Burnaby's framework designates Metrotown (south-west) as the city's downtown / regional city centre and this area's main shopping destination, and the quadrant's library branch is the Bob Prittie Metrotown Branch.

items.t: "Deer Lake Place" is the GVR board sub-area name as used in the SnapStats GVR report for Burnaby. Deer Lake Place is the small residential pocket at the west end of Deer Lake in central Burnaby, off Deer Lake Parkway near Gilpin Street, beside Burnaby's civic and cultural precinct at Deer Lake Park. "Deer Lake Place" is also a street / complex naming in the pocket; City use of the name as a neighbourhood name was not confirmed.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Deer Lake Place

items.t: Plans and hazards: the Burnaby 2050 Official Community Plan, adopted December 9, 2025, replaces the 1998 OCP and takes precedence over older community-plan land use maps where they conflict; community plans are adopted by Council as policy guidelines for rezoning and development applications. The pocket sits at the west end of Deer Lake beside its shoreline wetlands, so parcel-level streamside setbacks, floodplain and hazard status are property-specific checks: UNVERIFIED for individual lots; ALR status for a specific property is checked in the Agricultural Land Commission's ALR Property and Map Finder.

Burnaby property taxes and utilities: 2026 taxes were due Friday, July 3, 2026; a 5% penalty applies to outstanding current taxes (and to an unclaimed home owner grant) after the July due date, with a further 5% penalty after the September due date; Council approved a 2.9% property tax increase in the 2026–2030 Financial Plan, about $61 for the average home. The 2026 residential utility notice covers annual water, annual sewer use, a cross-connection device charge where applicable, and a residential garbage toter fee; the detached single-family dwelling water charge is $652.33, rates carry a 5% discount if paid by the due date, and for single-family homes sewer is billed as a sewer parcel tax on the property tax notice.

blocks.text: Good to know about Deer Lake Place

items.t: Burnaby's rulebook changed under this pocket twice in two years. The R1 SSMUH district arrived in June 2024, the Burnaby 2050 OCP was adopted December 9, 2025 (replacing the 1998 OCP and overriding older community-plan maps where they conflict), and the Burnaby Zoning Bylaw 2026 took effect July 1, 2026 — any Deer Lake Place document still citing the 1965 Zoning Bylaw No. 4742 or the 1998 OCP is two generations out of date.
Zero attached stock is a standing condition, not a slow month — and zero solds is separate again.

There is no mall, recreation centre or library branch inside the pocket. Burnaby Public Library's branch serving this quadrant is the Bob Prittie Metrotown Branch, and Metrotown — designated the city's downtown / regional city centre — is the pocket's shopping destination, south-west at the end of Gilpin Street's run toward Kingsway.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Deer Lake Place
Fee-simple lots

items.t: Established house lots: Freehold detached is the September 2026 record; the pocket's longer-run strata / freehold split: UNVERIFIED.

Lot character from the zone, as stated: the low-density lots around the pocket sit in Burnaby's R1 Small-Scale Multi-Unit Housing (SSMUH) District — Burnaby consolidated its former single- and two-family districts into R1 in June 2024: R1 lots may hold 3 units on lots up to 280 m², 4 units on larger lots, and 6 units on lots of at least 281 m² within 400 m of a frequent-transit stop, and lots with two or more primary units may be stratified; SSMUH lots require a minimum lot width of 10 m and minimum lot area of 281 m². Typical Deer Lake Place lot sizes at sub-area level: UNVERIFIED — the R1 thresholds above are the zone frame, not a claim about any existing lot's size.

Serviced position: Burnaby's 2026 residential utility notice covers annual water, annual sewer use, a cross-connection device charge where applicable, and a residential garbage toter fee; the detached single-family dwelling water charge is $652.33, rates carry a 5% discount if paid by the due date, and for single-family homes sewer is billed as a sewer parcel tax on the property tax notice. Servicing for any single vacant or redevelopment parcel is confirmed with the City, UNCONFIRMED parcel-by-parcel here.
ALR vs non-ALR: no ALR parcel in the pocket is confirmed in the research — no ALR split is stated, and ALR status for a specific property is checked in the ALC's ALR Property and Map Finder.

Hazard / setback position: the pocket sits at the west end of Deer Lake beside its shoreline wetlands; parcel-level streamside setbacks, floodplain and hazard status are property-specific checks: UNVERIFIED for individual lots.

items.t: Nearby areas: Deer Lake (around the lake and park) to the east, Buckingham Heights on the slope south-east of the lake, Burnaby Hospital to the north-west, Garden Village and Metrotown to the south-west. Canada Way runs to the north and Gilpin Street connects the pocket south toward Kingsway.

Civic anchors: Deer Lake Park is directly east — the City describes it as a peaceful natural environment that serves as the cultural centre of the city, with walking trails connecting the lake, Burnaby Art Gallery, Shadbolt Centre for the Arts, Burnaby Village Museum and Hart House restaurant, open dawn to dusk year-round at 6450 Deer Lake Ave; Burnaby City Hall is at 4949 Canada Way, just north-west of the pocket; Burnaby Hospital, 3935 Kincaid St, is immediately north-west.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Deer Lake Place

items.t: Subdivision + servicing requirements — base number held UNCONFIRMED (Burnaby precedent): subdivision parcel area, shape and dimensions must conform to the zoning bylaw for the parcel's zone, under the Burnaby Subdivision Control and Development Servicing Bylaw (renamed from the Burnaby Subdivision Control Bylaw 1971 by Amendment Bylaw No. 14667, 2024; the City's servicing updates took effect September 30, 2024). Required works and services include highways and lanes, water distribution connected to the City system, sewage collection and drainage collection, built to the City's Engineering Design Criteria Manual standards; the City's Servicing Improvements Guide addresses servicing for developments with four or more primary dwelling units on a residential lot.

Lakeshore diligence: the pocket sits beside Deer Lake's shoreline wetlands, so confirm streamside setbacks and any flood or hazard notation for the specific parcel before pricing redevelopment or an addition.

ALR rules (for completeness — no Deer Lake Place ALR parcel is confirmed here): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; SPA s. 239; ALCA s. 21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is three-tiered ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by Oct 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an ERROR. Check the parcel on ALC mapping before applying any of this.

The pocket's in-pocket school is not its catchment school: Deer Lake SDA School, 5550 Gilpin St, is an independent school on the Province's list — its presence in the pocket says nothing about the public catchment, which is address-based and UNVERIFIED here per address.

faq.q: Is Deer Lake Place the same as Deer Lake?
faq.a: No. In the SnapStats GVR report, Deer Lake, Deer Lake Place, Upper Deer Lake and Buckingham Heights are four separate Burnaby sub-areas with separate inventory and solds. Deer Lake Place is the small pocket at the west end of the lake, off Deer Lake Parkway near Gilpin Street (as of September 2026, Source: SnapStats GVR September 2026 report).

faq.q: What sold in Deer Lake Place in September 2026?
faq.a: Nothing: 0 solds on 10 detached listings, and no condos & townhomes listings at all, so the sales ratio is not applicable for either type. Burnaby-wide, the median detached sale price was $1,825,000 that month (as of September 2026, Source: SnapStats GVR September 2026 report).

faq.q: What is beside Deer Lake Place?
faq.a: Deer Lake Park, directly east — Burnaby's cultural centre, with the Shadbolt Centre for the Arts, Burnaby Art Gallery, Burnaby Village Museum, Hart House and the lake trails, open dawn to dusk year-round at 6450 Deer Lake Ave.

faq.q: Which schools serve a Deer Lake Place address?
faq.a: It depends on the address. The nearby public schools on the Province's SD41 list are Buckingham Elementary (K–7), 6066 Buckingham Ave, and Burnaby Central Secondary (8–12), 6011 Deer Lake Parkway; the school physically in the pocket, Deer Lake SDA at 5550 Gilpin St, is independent. Catchments are address-based and must be checked in the SD41 locator.

faq.q: Is there SkyTrain in Deer Lake Place?
faq.a: No station sits inside the pocket; Metrotown Station (Expo Line), south-west at Metrotown, is the nearest station for this pocket in the sources read.

faq.q: Is "Deer Lake Place" itself a condo complex?
faq.a: UNCONFIRMED. Ask for a strata plan number before treating any address as strata.

faq.q: Could a house lot here become strata units?
faq.a: Under the R1 SSMUH district, standard lots can hold 3–4 homes and larger lots near frequent transit up to 6, and lots with two or more primary units may be stratified — subject to the lakeshore-wetland setback checks for this pocket. Eligibility is lot-by-lot.

faq.q: Are there any townhomes in Deer Lake Place at all?
faq.a: A buyer set on townhouse living near the lake is shopping the neighbouring sub-areas, not this pocket.

faq.q: Is "Deer Lake Place" a strata complex I can buy into?
faq.a: UNCONFIRMED as a complex: the name is also a street / complex naming in the pocket, but no condo or townhome complex carrying it was confirmed on a developer or strata source. Do not treat the street name as a complex without a strata plan number.

faq.q: A portal shows Greentree Village townhouses as "near Deer Lake Place." Are they in this sub-area?
faq.a: No — Greentree Village is its own sub-area, the V5G pocket south of Canada Way behind BCIT/Deer Lake.

faq.q: Could a Deer Lake Place house lot become strata townhomes?
faq.a: Potentially, under the citywide R1 SSMUH district: 3 units on lots up to 280 m², 4 on larger lots, 6 on lots of at least 281 m² within 400 m of a frequent-transit stop, and lots with two or more primary units may be stratified — but lakeshore-wetland setback checks apply parcel by parcel under the Burnaby Zoning Bylaw 2026.

faq.q: Is there a vacant lot subdivision I can buy into in Deer Lake Place?
faq.a: No verified one — the pocket is established detached housing at the lake's west end; land trades as built house lots. No presale lot offering was verified.

faq.q: Can a Deer Lake Place lot be multiplexed or split?
faq.a: The citywide R1 rule allows 3–4 homes on a standard lot (6 only on a lot of at least 281 m² within 400 m of a frequent transit stop; minimum lot width 10 m, minimum lot area 281 m²) and multi-unit lots may be stratified — but the Burnaby 2050 OCP now governs over older maps, and lakeshore lots carry setback checks. Confirm zone, OCP designation and setback status for the parcel before pricing any split.
